text:
leo: quick note from onboarding run: magnet30B-int4hybrid shows a deterministic drift when prefill has contiguous numeric tokens (timestamps, IPs). happens near longctx boundary (~64k).

anya: deterministic drift how? output mismatch vs float baseline or kv index xor?

leo: both. on our eval harness i see: float baseline and int4hybrid diverge at token 65536 exactly (or +/-1 depending on prompt). kvcache fingerprints show slot collision: two different steps mapped to same slot id.

sam: that's worrying. i thought our shard address calc used 64-bit posacc; maybe quant clamp reduces precision. can you paste the minimal repro?

leo: reproduced with this tiny harness:
```
python -m tests.long_prefill_runner \
  --model magnet30B-int4hybrid \
  --prefill-file tests/prefills/timestamp_heavy.txt \
  --seed 0xdeadbeef \
  --ctx 66000 \
  --write-fingerprint=out/fp_run.json
```
prefill file is basically 10 lines of ISO times and a few numeric IP-like tokens.

faye: any recent change to the rotary embedding scaling or pos-embedding quant path? last week we merged per-head norm for magnet families.

leo: per-head norm landed in def-rotary-rescale (commit ff9a2). int4hybrid quant path also got a new bias folding step (commit ff9a8). combined looks suspicious.

harry: can we quickly test two hypotheses: (A) quantized poscalc loses precision and rounds down -> same slot; (B) bias folding changes token logits such that beam search alignment differs and flips the write timing.

anya: try A first by forcing high-precision poscalc at runtime: `POS_CALC_MODE=fp64 ./scripts/onboard_prefill.sh ...`

infra-bot: run queued on gpu-dedicated-7 (job id: job-99101).

leo: ran fp64 poscalc experiment. mismatch disappears for the deterministic case. so pos rounding is prime suspect.

sam: good narrow. next: where is poscalc performed in int4hybrid path? pre-kernel or in fused attention kernel?

leo: pre-kernel stage, inside quant_pos_utils.cu. i dumped the intermediate pos array for steps 65530-65540.

leo: snippet:
```
# step,pos_fp64,pos_int4_approx
65534,65534.000000,65534
65535,65535.000000,65535
65536,65536.000000,65536
65537,65537.000000,65537
```
but the int4 path applies a final right-shift of 1 (fast path) when head_dim % 64 == 0 (optimization from ff9a8). that shift is likely losing the LSB for large pos values.

faye: ah the 1-bit shift micro-optimization re: SIMD packing. that could alias pos 65536->32768 depending on packing math.

harry: can you try disabling that micro-opt at runtime? iirc we have ENABLE_POS_PACKING env flag.

leo: toggled: `ENABLE_POS_PACKING=0 ./tests/run_long_prefill.sh ...` -> mismatch gone.

sam: so root cause: packing optimization + int4 quantization reduces poscalc resolution near boundary leading to kvcache address collisions. very brittle.

anya: action items:
- revert pos-packing micro-opt in int4hybrid until we implement a safe packing that preserves MSBs (owner: leo, PR)
- add unit test in onboarding smoke that includes numeric-heavy prefills and checks kvcache fingerprint monotonicity across the window (owner: faye)
- document perf/regression tradeoff in model-onboard checklist so teams don't enable packing blind (owner: sam)

leo: i'll open PR with revert+comment. also add a stress test that repeats the timestamp-heavy stream with different seeds to catch off-by-one alignment.

faye: for the test, prefer hashing full slot ids and asserting no duplicates across steps (simple). we can run it in CI under ONBOARD_INTEGRATION.

harry: long-term: consider using 128-bit pos accumulator or an adaptive packing that keeps a separate offset base when pos > 32k. more expensive but rare. add to tech-debt list.

leo: one more note: this only triggered because our prefill had dense numeric tokens that compress similarly in the tokenizer and produced sequence length exactly hitting boundary. random language rarely aligns like that. so it's a data-triggered edge-case.

sam: create issue and label P2/P1? model bring-up blocking? seems blocking for int4hybrid onboarding.

anya: creating issue #4328: "pos-packing collision with int4hybrid -> kvcache aliasing for numeric-heavy prefills". marking P1 for magnet30B-int4hybrid bring-up, assigning to leo/faye. links to job-99101 artifacts: s3://redwood-artifacts/job-99101/ and harness at s3://redwood-test-repro/magnet30b/int4hybrid/timestamp-heavy/

infra-bot: job-99101 finished, exit=0, artifacts uploaded.

leo: follow-up: PR #3510 opened to revert packing and adds the regression test. running CI now. will post updates in issue.

faye: nice triage. we should also add note to "onboard-checklist.md" to include at least one numeric-heavy and one code-heavy prefill set. subtle tokens like dates and IPs catch these micro-optimizations. :mag:

sam: agreed. thanks team. we'll keep the int4hybrid disabled for hosted for now until PR lands and soak completes.
